title: kv-cache-memory-rebalancer-eviction-policy-improvements
author: Morgan Ellis
description: Context: KV cache fragmentation and aggressive spillover were causing intermittent OOMs and elevated page-write amplification under mixed-sequence workloads. This caused higher tail latency and increased egress I/O on machines with constrained device memory. Motivation: Improve memory utilization and reduce spillover churn without sacrificing request latency or throughput. Goals: (1) Reduce spillover page writes and fragmentation, (2) Introduce a lightweight memory rebalancer to prioritize hot KV entries and coalesce fragments, (3) Provide tunable eviction priorities for mixed workloads and per-deployment policies, (4) Maintain or improve latency P50/P95 for continuous batching. Changes in this PR: - Added a memory rebalancer component (runtime/kv_cache/rebalancer.*) that runs as a low-priority background task. The rebalancer: (a) coalesces adjacent free regions to reduce fragmentation, (b) promotes hot prefixes into contiguous slots when possible, (c) moves cold entries to spillover tiers proactively to avoid reactive evictions. - Introduced a two-tier spillover policy: fast-spill (low-latency spill to DRAM-backed page cache) and bulk-spill (batched writes to NVMe). The runtime now selects the tier based on recent I/O budget and expected eviction impact. - Eviction heuristics update: combine LRU score with a fragmentation penalty and request-hotness score. Added a pluggable scoring weight config (kv.cache.eviction.weights) with safe defaults. - Scheduling: rebalancer runs cooperatively with continuous-batching thread pool and yields when batch latency budget is tight. - New metrics and tracing points: kv_rebalancer_runs_total, kv_coalesced_bytes, kv_spill_fast_bytes, kv_spill_bulk_bytes, kv_eviction_score_distribution. - New unit/integration tests to cover rebalancer correctness, eviction ordering, and spillover tier selection. - Documentation updates: runtime/kv_cache/README.md with tuning knobs and recommended presets for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Risk and mitigation: rebalancer runs in background and is capped by CPU and I/O budget; added feature flag kv.rebalancer.enabled (off by default for 1.0 rollout) and a safe-mode that disables proactive moves if spill I/O exceeds configured threshold. Testing and results: Microbenchmarks (mixed short/long sequences) show ~18% reduction in spillover page writes and 12% lower OOM incidence in stressed runs compared to baseline, P95 latency unchanged (+/-1ms) and throughput steady (+3-4%). End-to-end canary on Dedicated with 48-hour run showed stable behavior; the feature was rolled out behind the flag. Rollout plan: - Step 1: Merge behind feature flag (this PR). - Step 2: Enable in Canary pool for 24-48h with kv.rebalancer.enabled=true and I/O budget at 40%. - Step 3: Gradually increase exposure and tune kv.cache.eviction.weights based on kv_eviction_score_distribution. Checklist: - [x] Implementation - rebalancer, eviction weights, two-tier spill - [x] Unit tests - rebalancer correctness - [x] Integration tests - spill tier selection - [x] Metrics + docs - [x] Canary verification - 48h Dedicated canary Notes: This description is a single continuous string and includes motivation, design summary, testing and rollout notes.
